svg.text: Stage Ready — architecture, as built (2026-09-20)
OpenCV 5 does the seeing, an agent decides, the loop enforces. Colour says where a thing runs:
on AWS (us-east-1)
on the laptop (macOS), cache-backed on S3 — not on AWS
browser
the loop
S3 read / write, keyed by source SHA-256
Browser — public endpoint (CloudFront)
https://d4nh99blf9f5j.cloudfront.net/ · drop a recording: fingerprinted (SHA-256) in the browser
?demo=1 (default) cached replay: fixtures recorded from measurement; no model, no OpenCV
?demo=0 the live hybrid below, streamed over SSE (keepalives) · Trace and Details drawers
UI and stills from S3 public/ through an origin access control; video with range requests
API Lambda — stage-ready-web
Python + Lambda Web Adapter, response streaming, IAM-only URL behind a CloudFront OAC.
Serves the UI, /api/clips, /api/recognize, /api/run/<id> (SSE) — and runs the loop with
the cached backend (?demo=1) or the live backend (?demo=0).
INSPECT — OpenCV 5 on Lambda (stage-ready-measure)
arm64, opencv-python-headless 5.0.0.93 as a layer; the workdir mirrored from S3 work/<sha>/
• picture-area detection (dead rows and columns) • pose coverage, one subject, steadiness
• framing dry solve: head target and size cap on one shared ruler • face exposure, key side
• OpenCV 5 DNN U²-Net subject opinion (cv2.dnn) — the matte's second opinion
• evidence-sufficiency: a recorded crown on ≥ 50 % of frames, or the head metrics are untrusted
live on every lineup recording (2026-09-19/20); the same code recomputes every fixture: 0 disagreements
DECIDE — Amazon Bedrock, Claude Sonnet 4.6
Converse with a forced `decide` tool: action ∈ {inspect, fix, process, deliver, reshoot}, a strategy
from the profile's allowed list, reasoning with the numbers, cited finding and gate ids.
Guardrails in code, not in the prompt: every process is verified, every fix re-inspected, deliver
refused unless the latest verification passed, retry budget 2; a refused decision is recorded
and falls through to the reshoot exit. The model is one environment variable.
FIX — fix.reframe, deterministic OpenCV on the Lambda
crop to the measured picture area; size-capped reframe solve (head pushed down, never up);
0 pixels invented; always re-inspected — a fix that creates a new defect is rejected
PROCESS — the Red Curtain render, on the laptop (cache-backed, not on AWS)
BodyTrack (Apple Vision pose) · MatAnyone 2 (PyTorch, MPS) · crown completion · track_frame ·
Composite (CoreImage) · ffmpeg. process.standard = a cache hit on the archived run; the
separation-targeted retry re-composites at the strategy's bounds and uploads to artifacts/<sha>/.
details in the right column · a fresh upload has no workdir yet, and the loop says so
VERIFY — OpenCV 5 on Lambda, against the profile's 9 gates
on the composite frames and the delivered file, mirrored from S3:
• separation: edge luma inside / outside ≥ 1.5× • matte extent vs the DNN opinion ≥ 0.9
• head stability: spread ≤ 2 %, drift ≤ 4 px • crown evidence ≥ 50 % • pose, one subject
• frame count = source • audio MD5 = source (audio identity)
not measured: frozen / repeated-frame motion continuity — a stated limitation
every record written to measurements/<sha>/ on S3
Input video + Target Output Profile
profiles/midtown_red_curtain.json — 1080×1920 canvas, the framing rule, 9 gates, the allowed
strategies with their bounds, retry budget 2, reshoot guidance per finding. A second destination
would be a second profile file; only this one exists today.
A recording is recognised by its SHA-256 (sources/<sha>/); an unknown upload is told so.
S3 — stage-ready-videos (private; public access blocked)
sources/<sha256>/source.mp4 the recording, keyed by its own hash
work/<sha256>/… pose track, seed, matte, composite frames, logs
artifacts/<sha256>/attempt_N.mp4 the deliveries
measurements/<sha256>/*.json every INSPECT / VERIFY record
runs/<sha256>/<run_id>/trace.jsonl the run's trace
models/u2net_human_seg.onnx the DNN weights, hash-checked
public/ UI + stills, read by CloudFront through an OAC
Provenance: every derived input carries its original's and its own SHA-256 and the
exact command (demo/derived.json); a controlled input says so on the page.
Trace / observability
Every Lambda invocation and Bedrock call: request id, latency, tokens, model, stop reason;
every finding, decision (reasoning + citations), fix, stage, gate and error → trace.jsonl on
S3 and .stage_ready/runs/ locally; streamed live into the UI's Trace drawer. No credentials,
no performer media in any log. A live run costs ≈ $0.07 (Lambda + Bedrock).
Evaluation: 19 labelled items, blind; agent vs rule table vs the linear pipeline (evaluate).
Cached demo (?demo=1) vs live hybrid (?demo=0) — same loop, same interface
Cached: demo/clips/<id>/*.json — the inspect, fix, process and verify records written by
`record` from the live OpenCV 5 measurement; the agent's decisions cached in its own words;
replayed deterministically by the API Lambda. Three sample cases in the picker.
Live: INSPECT / FIX / VERIFY on the measurement Lambda, DECIDE on Bedrock, PROCESS a cache
hit from S3 keyed on the source hash — 3 to 6 minutes per recording, every step traced.
`python3 -m stage_ready measure` prints every fixture number beside its recomputation
DELIVER
RETRY
separation-targeted, in budget
RESHOOT
cited causes + guidance
Only the loop owns the exits: deliver needs a passing verification; a reshoot request leads with the
findings the agent cited as the cause, each with the profile's guidance for the next recording.
The retry re-processes with the one strategy that addresses the failing gate, then verifies again.
The Red Curtain pipeline — macOS, cache-backed on S3
Runs on the laptop; its outputs are what the Lambda measures. Not on AWS today.
1. picture area (OpenCV) → band frames
2. BodyTrack — Apple Vision body pose → pose track
3. pose QC — coverage, one subject, steadiness (refused below 60 % coverage)
4. seed — Apple Vision person matte on a picked frame, cleaned (or U²-Net)
5. MatAnyone 2 (PyTorch, MPS) — the video matte, keyed on source+seed hash
6. crown completion from the performer's own uncut frames (carve if none)
7. track_frame — the reframe solve on the shared ruler (head target, size cap)
8. auto-grade + Composite (CoreImage) — the graded stage render, plate untouched
9. ffmpeg — H.264, source audio copied; frame count and audio MD5 checked
process.standard: the archived run, a cache hit. separation_targeted: the same
matte and tracking, re-composited at the bounds (rim 0.45, wrap 0.70, lift +0.04).
Synced to S3 by hash: `aws sync <clip>` — work/, sources/, artifacts/.
Planned: fresh-upload workdirs and cloud rendering (README roadmap).
Planned, not built: this stage on AWS compute — the three tools are macOS.
Second Target Output Profile: planned, not yet validated.
Tooling on the laptop
`record` — a clip's fixtures from the measurement, not by hand
`measure` — every fixture number recomputed with OpenCV 5, side by side
`evaluate` — the labelled set through the real loop, both agents, the report
`aws sync | deploy | web-deploy` — S3 by hash, the two Lambdas, CloudFront
`demo/derive.sh`, `demo/eval/derive_eval.sh` — derived inputs with provenance
`bundle` — the judge archive for what the repo does not ship (performer media)
Red Curtain archive (~/mts)
The show's pipeline and its measured workdirs. Everything the demo replays was
measured here first, then again on the Lambda — the numbers agree (README,
"What is measured"). Media lives here and on S3, never in the repository.
judge access: the private bundle, to be arranged at submission
retry → PROCESS with the strategy that addresses the failing gate → VERIFY again (budget 2)
what PROCESS runs →
S3
